record.title: Microsoft describes Project Perception as a control system for internal AI agents
record.summary: In an Oct 19 post, Microsoft Security EVP Hayete Gallot argues that enterprise AI agents should be treated as “agentic insiders” and says Project Perception can be applied to monitor and govern them. The post describes assigning agents identities, containers and permissions; estimating risk from signals; and using Guardian Agents to supervise and respond to actions. This is Microsoft’s account of an intended security approach and stated availability, not evidence of measured efficacy, broad deployment or independent validation.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_PUBLIC_ARTIFACT
claims.text: Microsoft published an Oct 19, 2026 post by Microsoft Security EVP Hayete Gallot titled “Securing the agentic insider.”

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Microsoft says Project Perception, previously announced in July, can be applied to enterprise agents by discovering them, assigning identity/containers/permissions, assessing action risk and using Guardian Agents to supervise and respond to actions in real time.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Microsoft says Project Perception is available to help organizations begin securing internal agents.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The post does not establish control accuracy, tested threat coverage, latency, independent evaluation, deployment scale or operational security outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The technical design and availability status of the described Project Perception controls were not established from the announcement alone.
No independent or customer evaluation of detection/response accuracy, latency, threat coverage or security outcomes was located in this review.

brief.importance_rationale: If operationalized as described, continuous identity-, permission- and risk-aware supervision of enterprise agents could affect enterprise security architecture as agent access to data and tools grows; the Oct 19 post gives no measured efficacy or deployment evidence, so the consequence claim is material but bounded.
limitations: The announcement is a high-level first-party description without technical artifacts, architecture details, evaluation results or quantified outcomes.
The post does not distinguish generally available capabilities from roadmap or advisory material in the linked getting-started page, which was not inspected in this activation.
No evidence here establishes that continuous action supervision detects or prevents agent misuse, or that the approach generalizes across enterprise deployments.
brief.summary: In an Oct 19 post, Microsoft Security EVP Hayete Gallot argues that enterprise AI agents should be treated as “agentic insiders” and says Project Perception can be applied to monitor and govern them. The post describes assigning agents identities, containers and permissions; estimating risk from signals; and using Guardian Agents to supervise and respond to actions. This is Microsoft’s account of an intended security approach and stated availability, not evidence of measured efficacy, broad deployment or independent validation.

technical.claimed_result: Microsoft presents Project Perception as a way to monitor and govern internal enterprise agents through identity/permission controls, dynamic risk assessment and Guardian Agent supervision.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary artifact demonstrates that Microsoft publicly described this approach on Oct 19; it does not demonstrate the approach’s technical effectiveness.
technical.implementation_status: Microsoft says Project Perception was announced in July and can be applied to agentic insiders; detailed availability and deployment scope were not verified in this review.
technical.mechanism: The post describes collecting signals across identity, data, cloud, endpoint, network and runtime; assigning agents identities, containers and permissions; computing action risk; then using green/blue Guardian Agents to supervise and respond to actions.
technical.novelty: The post reframes internal enterprise agents as insider-risk subjects and applies Project Perception’s cyber-defense stack to their monitoring and governance; the technical implementation and novelty relative to existing agent-security tools are not established.
technical.regime: Enterprise agents with access to organizational data, tools, systems and critical processes, as described by Microsoft; no deployment cohort or tested threat model is provided.
technical.reproducibility: No technical artifacts or reproducible evaluation were included in the inspected post.
technical.strongest_baseline: No comparative baseline or measured security outcome is reported.

brief.title: Microsoft describes Project Perception as a control system for internal AI agents
brief.why_it_matters: If implemented as described, continuous identity-, permission- and risk-aware supervision could shape enterprise security architecture as agents receive access to data, tools and critical processes. The announcement does not establish how well the controls detect or contain misuse, what threat models they cover, or whether they are deployed at scale.
